description: Risk-based review routing. Not every change needs every reviewer; requiring all of them is how review becomes theatre. Routing is additive: a change matching several signals gets the union of reviewers.

routes.signal: only documentation, comments or non-executable assets changed
public interface, contract or schema changed
auth, crypto, secret handling, input parsing or deserialization touched
hot path, batch size, query pattern, concurrency or caching changed
retry, timeout, failover, queue, idempotency or health-check behaviour changed
CI/CD, container, infrastructure or deployment configuration changed
this repository's agents, skills, hooks, policies or schemas changed
routes.notes: agent-evaluator and ai-governance are deliberately spawnable by no delivery role. A change to this repository's own agents, hooks or policies is AP-10 work: the review is dispatched from the main session, not delegated down a line the change could itself alter.

rules: The author never reviews its own change. If the routed reviewer is the authoring role, the review escalates to that role's owner chapter.
A blocking gate with an unresolved HIGH or CRITICAL finding stops the merge.
Advisory gates surface findings without blocking.
Reviewers read the diff and the linked requirement, story and architecture artifacts. A review that cannot name what the change is for is not a review.
